description: TENET is a team of passionate innovators participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge, working on the challenge Lunar Landing Site Navigator. Our mission is to leverage space science, data analysis, and intelligent technology to identify safe and optimal landing sites on the Moon. By combining creativity, technical expertise, and teamwork, we aim to develop an innovative navigation solution that supports future lunar exploration and makes space missions safer and smarter.
summary:
Imagine standing on the Moon, where a few degrees of sunlight can determine the success of an entire mission, and losing sight of Earth could mean losing communication with home. This is the challenge our project aims to solve.

Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an interactive lunar mission-planning application designed to help astronauts, scientists, and mission planners identify and compare suitable landing locations, particularly near the Moon's south pole. By combining lunar location data, date and time selection, and scientific calculations, our tool visualizes the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to the lunar horizon.

Users can explore potential landing sites through interactive maps and 3D visualizations, evaluate solar elevation and sunlight availability for power generation, and identify direct-to-Earth communication windows. Our platform also enables side-by-side comparisons of different locations and landing dates, supported by clear timelines and visual indicators.

What makes our idea exciting is its ability to transform complex space science into an intuitive and engaging experience. We aim to bridge the gap between advanced scientific data and accessible technology, helping people understand the challenges of lunar exploration while supporting smarter, more informed mission planning.

Our vision: Making every landing decision smarter, every mission better prepared, and humanity's next giant leap towards the Moon a little closer.
details:
• What does it do or how does it work?
    TENET is an advanced web-based mission control and topographical navigation system designed for lunar exploration, focusing on lunar south polar landing sites (such as Shackleton Crater, Malapert Massif, and Nobile Rim). It operates via an interactive 3D WebGL Moon globe powered by Three.js, integrated with live NASA Lunar Mapping WMTS global mosaic tiles (LRO WAC) and LOLA (Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter) topography data. It dynamically computes selenocentric ephemeris, 29.5-day synodic solar cycles, Sun and Earth elevations, orbital mechanics, and local 360° horizon terrain occlusion masks to evaluate direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication and solar illumination windows.
    • Languages & UI: HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS, JavaScript (ES6+).
    • 3D Graphics & Rendering: Three.js (r128) WebGL rendering engine.
    • Data Sources & Ephemeris: NASA Lunar Mapping WMTS REST endpoints (LRO_WAC_Mosaic_Global_303ppd_v02), LOLA DEM 5m/azimuthal horizon profiles, and JPL Horizons-based selenocentric mechanics.
